items.gist: The passage presents prātibha realization, inward Śiva, and jīvanmukti as its fruit.
It contrasts bondage through elements and senses with liberation through prātibha and Śakti.
It argues that discrimination arises through Śiva's power, not through mind and intellect alone.
It distinguishes pure discrimination from the binding, inert senses.
It explains dīkṣā as cutting bonds and strengthening understanding through Śiva's teaching.
It describes Śaivī Śakti joining the soul and granting liberation according to fitness.
It presents intense descent leading the aspirant to a true guru and Śiva.
It questions temporal causation and affirms Śaivī power as the real cause.
It links Śakti's peace with dissolution of individuality and eventual bodily death.
It marks the end of the prior topic and lists signs of Rudra-Śakti possession.
It enumerates powers and introduces the second, clearer topic.
It describes moderate descent and the marks of a true guru.
It explains how aspiration leads to guru, purification, and immediate Śiva-giving dīkṣā.
It states that one who knows truth is liberated even while embodied.
It discusses liberation despite residual karma and the body's continued experience.
It presents mantra power and dīkṣā as cutting bonds and separating prāṇa.
It warns against untimely death-dīkṣā and concludes the śaktipāta discussion.
